releases.name: v1.18.1
releases.body:
## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.18.1

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Patch
* Aura API requests now identify the caller in the User-Agent header as `Neo4jCLI/<version> (agent|script|human)`, so Aura can tell agent-driven, scripted and interactive use apart.

releases.name: v1.18.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **Aura agent evaluations** — `aura agent evaluation-dataset` and `aura agent evaluation-run` let you build question sets and score an agent against them on accuracy, tool trajectory, groundedness and relevance, so you can see whether your agent is actually any good. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura agent evaluation-run create --agent-id <agent-id> --dataset-id <dataset-id> --metric accuracy --metric groundedness --wait --rw
  ```

### Other changes

- `neo4j-cli update` and `neo4j-cli update check` no longer fail with the GitHub API rate-limit error (HTTP 403, exit code 8): release metadata now comes from a static document on neo4j.sh, so no `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` is needed or read. Everything else is unchanged.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.18.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* Adds `aura agent evaluation-dataset` and `aura agent evaluation-run` commands for managing Aura agent evaluation datasets and runs
### Patch
* neo4j-cli update and neo4j-cli update check no longer fail with the GitHub API rate-limit error (HTTP 403 advising to set GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, exit code 8): release metadata is now fetched from a static document on neo4j.sh instead of the GitHub API, so no token is needed or read. Commands, flags, output, and exit codes are otherwise unchanged.

releases.name: v1.17.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **Desktop projects and tags** — `desktop project` and `desktop tag` now cover list/create/update/delete, and the new `desktop dbms update` (plus `--project`/`--tags` on `desktop connection update`) files things where they belong, so your local DBMSes no longer live in one big drawer. Heads-up: in `desktop` JSON output, `project` is now `projects` and it's an array. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli desktop dbms update my-dbms-id --project "Customer 360" --tags prod,eu --rw
  ```

- **`agent-context` goes on a diet** — the default output is now a compact command index (about 18 KB instead of about 465 KB), so agents can spend their context on your problem rather than our help text. Ask for one command's details by path, or pass `--full` for the old tree (`schema_version` is now 2). Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli agent-context aura instance list --format json
  ```

### Other changes

- Unknown flags and commands now print the error, a one-line usage and a `Run '<command> --help'` hint instead of the entire help text.
- `desktop list` and `desktop connection list` work again against Neo4j Desktop 2.3, which reports `createdAt` as a number.
- On Windows, the `skill` commands find installed agents when `HOME` is unset (via `%USERPROFILE%`), so `skill install --all` picks up Codex.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.17.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* New commands for managing projects and tags in a local Neo4j Desktop 2 install: `desktop project list/create/update/delete` and `desktop tag list/create/update/delete` manage the Desktop project and tag catalogs. Create and update print the changed entry, failing with an error if Desktop's returned catalog state lacks it; delete prints a minimal confirmation envelope (`id` and `deleted: true`). The new `desktop dbms update` command renames a DBMS, edits its description, or replaces its project/tag assignments. `desktop connection update` gains matching `--project`/`--tags` flags; both take project/tag names or UUIDs (repeatable/comma-separated) with replace semantics, and an empty value clears the assignments. In `desktop` JSON output, the `project` field on DBMS and connection objects is renamed to `projects` and is now an array instead of a single string. On Desktop versions too old to have the projects/tags endpoints, these commands fail with a clear message telling the user to upgrade Neo4j Desktop 2.
* agent-context now prints a compact command index (about 18 KB instead of about 465 KB) by default; pass a command path (e.g. `agent-context aura instance list`) for that command's details, or --full for the previous complete tree. schema_version is now 2 and `commands` is a flat list of path/short entries by default.
### Patch
* Unknown flags and unknown commands now print the error, a one-line usage and a `Run '<command> --help'` hint instead of the full help text with all examples.
* Fixed `desktop list` and `desktop connection list` failing against Neo4j Desktop 2.3, which reports a connection's `createdAt` as a numeric timestamp instead of a string.
* On Windows, `skill install`, `skill list`, `skill remove` and `skill check` now detect installed agents when the `HOME` environment variable is unset (home is resolved from `%USERPROFILE%`), so `skill install --all` works for Codex users (bundled with ChatGPT Desktop on Windows).

releases.name: v1.16.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **`aura instance create` and `aura instance deploy` drop `--version`** — Aura's create endpoint now picks the Neo4j version itself and rejects requests that try to set one, so the flag has gone. If a script still passes `--version`, delete it and the script works again. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura instance create --name my-free-db --type free --rw --format json
  ```

### Other changes

- Usage analytics events now include the parent process binary name (`pprocess_binary`) when it can be found. It's the file name only, with no directory, so your home path stays out of it.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.16.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* `aura instance create` and `aura instance deploy` no longer accept the `--version` flag
* Usage analytics events now include the name of the parent process binary that launched the CLI (`pprocess_binary`, file name only, no directory), when it can be determined

releases.name: v1.15.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **`docker create --plugin`** — Spin up a local container with APOC or Graph Data Science already installed, instead of installing them by hand afterwards. Repeat the flag or pass a comma-separated list. A misspelt name surfaces in `docker logs <name>`, since the image is the one that installs plugins. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli docker create --name gds --plugin apoc --plugin graph-data-science --rw
  ```

- **Ctrl-C now stops things** — In-flight Aura requests and `--wait` polling are cancelled when you press Ctrl-C, so the command exits with 130 (143 for SIGTERM) and doesn't keep going. Press Ctrl-C a second time to force-quit. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura instance create --type free --wait --rw
  ```

- **`docker delete --remove-volume`** — Containers made by `docker load` leave their loaded database in a `neo4j-cli-<name>-data` volume, and you can now remove it in the same step. On a terminal you're asked (default no). With `--yes --force` the volume is kept and the cleanup command is printed. The CLI only ever removes the volume it created itself. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli docker delete movies --remove-volume --yes --force --rw
  ```

### Other changes

- If the Aura API or its auth endpoint can't be reached, times out or sends an unreadable response, Aura commands now exit 8 (retryable) with an error. They used to crash and exit 0.
- An unexpected internal crash now exits 1 and writes to stderr. It used to exit 0 on stdout, which made failures look like successes.
- A corrupt or unreadable `config.json` now gives a clear error that names the file (exit 1) instead of crashing.
- `docker create` no longer leaves a running container with a lost password. Credential-store problems now fail before the container starts. `docker load` and `aura instance load` run the same checks.
- `aura agent` commands now report a missing organization or project with the standard default-workspace usage error (exit 2). `--organization-id` / `--project-id` are now documented once, on the `agent` group.
- Aura commands now reject resource IDs containing path or query characters (`/`, `..`, `?`, `#`) before sending a request.
- `neo4j-cli docker` now works when `docker` is aliased to podman. Listing containers used to fail on podman's JSON format.
- `aura graph-analytics session list` now fetches every page of sessions, not just the first.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.15.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* `docker create` gains `--plugin` (repeatable, or comma-separated) to install Neo4j plugins such as `apoc` or `graph-data-science` in the new container via `NEO4J_PLUGINS`; the command's result lists them. Plugin names are lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, and a name the image does not know shows up in `docker logs <name>` when the container starts.
* Pressing Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or sending SIGTERM now stops a running command promptly: in-flight Aura requests and `--wait` polling are cancelled instead of running to completion, and the command exits with status 130 (143 for SIGTERM). A second Ctrl-C force-quits.
* `docker delete` can now remove the data volume that a `docker load` container leaves behind (`neo4j-cli-<name>-data`, which holds the loaded database): pass `--remove-volume`, or answer the new prompt on a terminal (default no). With `--yes --force` and no `--remove-volume` the volume is kept and the command to remove it later is printed. Only the volume the CLI created for that container is ever removed.
### Patch
* Aura commands no longer crash and exit 0 when the Aura API or its authentication endpoint cannot be reached, times out, or sends an unreadable response. They now report an error and exit 8 (upstream, retryable), and Aura commands reject a malformed API response with an error instead of crashing.
* An unexpected internal crash now exits with status 1 (it previously exited 0, so a failed command could look successful) and prints its diagnostic to stderr instead of stdout.
* A corrupt or unreadable `config.json` now produces a clear error naming the file (exit 1) instead of a crash.
* `docker create` no longer leaves a running container whose password is lost. A missing credential store, or a reserved or already-stored credential name (for example `desktop`), now fails before the container is created. If storing the credential fails after the container starts, the password is still shown with a warning; with `--no-print-password` and a generated password the container is removed and the command fails. `docker load` and `aura instance load` apply the same checks.
* `aura agent` commands now report a missing organization or project with the standard `no organization specified; set a default workspace ...` usage error (exit 2) instead of `required flag(s) ... not set`, and the `--organization-id` and `--project-id` flags are documented once on the `agent` group instead of on every subcommand.
* Aura commands now reject organization, project, agent, instance, GraphQL Data API, authentication-provider, virtual-graph, session, snapshot and customer-managed-key IDs that contain path or query characters (such as `/`, `..`, `?` or `#`), with a validation error, before sending any request.
* The `docker` commands now work when `docker` is aliased to podman. Listing containers (used by `docker create`, `list`, `get` and `load`) failed with a JSON parse error because podman reports container names and labels in a different shape.
* `aura graph-analytics session list` now returns all pages of sessions instead of only the first server-defaulted page, so sessions beyond that first page are no longer missing from the output.

releases.name: v1.14.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **`EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` finally show you the plan** — the query planner's output is no longer swallowed: `--format json` and `--format toon` carry it as a structured `plan`/`profile` object, and `--format table` prints it as an indented operator tree, with `PROFILE` also reporting per-operator rows, dbHits and time. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli query "PROFILE MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p)" --format table
  ```

- **`EXPLAIN` of a write no longer needs `--rw`** — `EXPLAIN` never executes the statement, so making you opt in to writes just to look at a plan was a false alarm. `PROFILE` does execute, so a `PROFILE` of a write is still refused without `--rw`. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli query "EXPLAIN CREATE (:Person {name: 'Alice'})" --format json
  ```


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.14.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* query now shows the execution plan for EXPLAIN and PROFILE statements: --format json/toon carry it as a plan or profile object, and --format table prints it as an indented operator tree (PROFILE also reporting per-operator rows, dbHits and time). EXPLAIN of a statement that writes no longer requires --rw (EXPLAIN never executes); PROFILE of a statement that writes is still refused without --rw.

releases.name: v1.13.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **`update` now tells you what you just installed** — self-updating no longer leaves you guessing: after a successful swap the CLI prints the release notes for every version you jumped over, newest first, capped at the three most recent (with a link to the full changelog when older releases are trimmed). `--no-changelog` if you prefer the strong, silent type, and `--format json` / `--format toon` gain a `release_notes` field plus `changelog_url`. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli update
  ```

- **`mcp install` writes an env block, so capability gates actually work** — in config mode the write / Aura / credential gates were previously unreachable without `--bundle`; now the entry carries the env block that switches them on. A typed `--rw` enables all three, or scope them individually with the new `--allow-writes`, `--allow-aura`, and `--allow-credential-write`. In bundle mode the flags seed the extension's settings toggles instead of being quietly ignored, and `mcp check` reports an older entry missing the env block as drift. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli mcp install --agent claude-desktop --rw --allow-writes
  ```

### Other changes

- `graphql cors-policy allowed-origin add` / `remove` return a clear error (exit 8) instead of panicking when the data API answers with an unexpected 2xx status or a malformed CORS policy body, and authorization failures no longer ask you to report an issue that isn't one.
- `docker create --no-print-password` help text stops pointing at a credential-read command that never existed; it now explains connecting via `--credential <name>` and resetting the password with `admin user set-password` plus a credential resync.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.13.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* `neo4j-cli update` now prints the release notes for the versions between the old and new version after a successful update, newest first and capped at the 3 most recent (with a link to the full changelog when older releases are omitted). Pass `--no-changelog` to suppress it. `--format json` and `--format toon` gain a `release_notes` field, plus `changelog_url` when releases were omitted; `--format table` is unchanged.
### Patch
* Updated `docker create --no-print-password` help text to no longer reference a credential-read command that does not exist. Now explains how to use the stored credential via `--credential <name>` and how to reset the password with `admin user set-password` plus a credential resync.
* `mcp install` now writes an env block, so write / Aura / credential access actually works with Claude Desktop in config mode (previously unreachable without --bundle). A typed `--rw` enables all three gates; the new `--allow-writes`, `--allow-aura`, and `--allow-credential-write` flags scope them individually. In bundle mode the flags seed the extension settings toggles instead of being ignored. `mcp check` reports a pre-existing entry without the env block as drift.
* graphql cors-policy allowed-origin add/remove now return a clear error (exit 8) instead of panicking when the data API responds with an unexpected 2xx status or a malformed CORS policy body, and authorization failure messages no longer say 'please report an issue'.

releases.name: v1.12.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **`aura api` reaches any Aura endpoint the CLI has no command for** — the endpoint carries its own version segment, `{org_id}`/`{project_id}` are filled in from your flags or default workspace, and `--format json` writes the body byte-for-byte so `jq` can have it. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura api 'v2beta1/organizations/{org_id}/projects' --format json
  ```
  Non-GET/HEAD methods need `--rw`, and DELETE also wants confirmation — the escape hatch is not a trapdoor.

- **New `mcp` command group for agents that can't run commands themselves** — exposes five tools (target discovery, command listing, docs, read-only run, write run) to MCP clients like Claude Desktop; write, Aura and credential access are each off by default. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli config set flag.mcp-server true --rw
  neo4j-cli mcp install --agent claude-desktop --bundle --rw
  ```
  If your agent can already shell out, `neo4j-cli skill install` remains the better fit.

- **Instance creation accepts tier names again** — `create`, `deploy` and `load` now take `free`, `professional`, `business-critical` and `virtual-dedicated-cloud`, the names the API actually asks for. Previously no value worked at all: the old `*-db` names passed the CLI and were rejected by the API, and the API's names were rejected by the CLI. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura instance create --rw --name my-instance --type professional --cloud-provider aws --region us-east-1 --memory 1GB
  ```
  The former names still work and are mapped across; `professional-ds` and `enterprise-ds` are gone and now say so by name.

### Other changes

- `--graph-analytics-plugin` on a professional instance now actually enables GDS, instead of being silently ignored while every instance defaulted to serverless.
- Aura commands report the API's own message and a non-zero exit code for HTTP 413, 415, 422 and friends, rather than a "please report an issue" note with a success exit code; empty or non-JSON 4xx/5xx bodies keep their status-class exit code too.
- `aura instance list` now includes `organization_id` alongside `project_id`, so the owning organization no longer needs a second lookup.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.12.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* New `neo4j-cli aura api <endpoint>` command makes an authenticated request to any Aura API endpoint and prints the response. The endpoint carries its own API version segment (`v1/instances`, `v2beta1/organizations/{org_id}/projects`), and `{org_id}`/`{project_id}` are substituted from `--organization-id`/`--project-id` or the default workspace. Supports `--method`/`-X`, repeatable `--field`/`-F` and `--raw-field`/`-f` (query parameters on GET/HEAD/DELETE, a JSON body otherwise), `--input` for a verbatim body from a file or stdin, repeatable `--header`/`-H`, plus `--include`/`-i` and `--silent`. Non-GET/HEAD methods require `--rw` and DELETE also requires confirmation (`--yes --force` when non-interactive). With `--format json` the response body is written byte-for-byte so it can be piped into `jq`; a failing status yields the usual error envelope and exit code.
* New `neo4j-cli mcp` command group (`serve`, `tool`, `install`, `remove`, `list`, `check`, `bundle`) behind the `flag.mcp-server` feature flag (`NEO4J_CLI_FLAG_MCP_SERVER=1` or `neo4j-cli config set flag.mcp-server true`). This targets agents and chat surfaces with no filesystem or shell access, which therefore cannot invoke `neo4j-cli` themselves — Claude Desktop being the reference client. Agents that can already run commands are better served by `neo4j-cli skill install`. Exposes the CLI through five tools: `neo4j_cli_list_targets` (discovers reachable Neo4j databases), `neo4j_cli_list_commands` (lists CLI command trees), `neo4j_cli_read_docs` (returns documentation from the generated skill bundle), `neo4j_cli_run` (executes read-only CLI commands), and `neo4j_cli_run_write` (executes destructive CLI commands, requires `--rw`). To install into Claude Desktop, run `neo4j-cli config set flag.mcp-server true` then `neo4j-cli mcp install --agent claude-desktop --bundle --rw`, which generates a `.mcpb` bundle and opens the Desktop install UI; omit `--bundle` to write `mcpServers."neo4j-cli"` directly into `claude_desktop_config.json`. Write, Aura and credential access are each off by default and are enabled per-connector in the Desktop settings UI.
* The `aura instance list` output now includes an `organization_id` field alongside `project_id`, so the owning organization of each instance is visible without a separate lookup.
### Patch
* Aura commands now report the API's own error message and a non-zero exit code for HTTP 413, 415, 422 and other previously unhandled statuses, instead of a "please report an issue" message with a success exit code. A 4xx or 5xx whose body is empty or not JSON now also keeps its status-class exit code rather than reporting a generic internal failure.
* `aura instance create`, `deploy` and `load` now accept the Aura tier names the API expects: `--type free`, `professional`, `business-critical` and `virtual-dedicated-cloud`. Previously no value worked — `free-db`/`professional-db`/`enterprise-db` passed the CLI's own check but were rejected by the API with a `validation_error`, while the names the API asked for were rejected by the CLI as invalid arguments. The former names are still accepted and mapped to their current equivalents; `professional-ds` and `enterprise-ds` no longer exist and are now rejected with a message naming the replacement. `customer-managed-key create --type` is unchanged and still takes the former names.
* instance create/deploy/load: --graph-analytics-plugin on a professional instance now actually enables the GDS plugin (graph_analytics: plugin). Previously the flag was silently ignored by the v2beta1 API and every professional instance defaulted to graph_analytics: serverless regardless of the flag.

releases.name: v1.11.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **`neo4j-cli admin` — the whole administration tree lands at once** — four new subtrees for managing a Neo4j DBMS over Bolt via the system database, with full connection-flag parity with `query` (`--uri`, `--username`, `--password`, `--credential`, `--env`, `--debug`):
  - `admin database` — list, get, create, drop, start, stop, with `--wait` polling on the lifecycle commands.
  - `admin user` — list, get, create, drop, rename, set-password, suspend, activate.
  - `admin role` — list, get, create, drop, grant, revoke.
  - `admin privilege` — `grant`/`deny`/`revoke` each with a per-category subcommand (property, entity, graph, label, load, database, dbms) taking the action as a positional argument, plus `admin privilege list`. For example: `neo4j-cli admin privilege grant property read --on-graph '*' --role analyst`.

- **Credential env vars now require opt-in via `accept-env-vars`** — the CLI no longer reads credentials out of the environment behind your back; when you do enable it, precedence is uniformly flag > env var > stored, across Aura, DBMS and embed credentials. Partial sets are rejected with a missing-variable error instead of quietly falling back. **Breaking:** DBMS and embed env vars (covering `query` and the entire `admin` tree), plus the `NEO4J_DATABASE` override alongside `--credential`, are ignored until this is on. The explicit `--database` flag is unaffected, and stored credentials are never modified. Set `NEO4J_CLI_ACCEPT_ENV_VARS=1` for zero-setup CI with no config file at all. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli config set accept-env-vars true --rw
  ```

- **`aura virtual-graph` for Aura Virtual Graphs** — `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `delete` and `allowed-configs` for virtual graphs in a project. `create` prints the initial password exactly once as `plain_password`, so do read the output. `list` follows the API's pagination on your behalf and mentions on stderr when `--limit` hid something from you. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura virtual-graph create --rw --name sales-analytics --data-source-id ds-abc123 --import-model-id im-xyz789 --cloud-provider gcp --region europe-west1
  ```

### Other changes

- `aura instance list` output now includes the instance `status`.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.11.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* Add `neo4j-cli admin database` commands for database lifecycle management (list, get, create, drop, start, stop) with full connection flag parity with `query`
* add admin user management commands (list, get, create, drop, rename, set-password, suspend, activate)
* Add admin role commands: list, get, create, drop, grant, revoke
* Add admin privilege commands for managing Neo4j Enterprise privileges via the system database. `grant`/`deny`/`revoke` each expose a per-category subcommand (property, entity, graph, label, load, database, dbms) taking the action as a positional argument (e.g. `admin privilege grant property read --on-graph * --role analyst`), plus `admin privilege list`
* Add a global `accept-env-vars` config key (default `false`) that gates whether the CLI reads credentials from environment variables. Set it with `neo4j-cli config set accept-env-vars true --rw`, or set `NEO4J_CLI_ACCEPT_ENV_VARS=1` for zero-setup CI usage with no config file. When enabled, env vars override stored credentials at the precedence flag > env var > stored, uniformly across Aura (`NEO4J_AURA_CLIENT_ID`/`NEO4J_AURA_CLIENT_SECRET`, now synthesized into an ephemeral in-memory credential), DBMS (`NEO4J_URI`/`NEO4J_USERNAME`/`NEO4J_PASSWORD`/`NEO4J_DATABASE`), and embed (`NEO4J_EMBED_*`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `HF_TOKEN`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`) credentials; partial sets are rejected with a missing-variable error. BREAKING: DBMS and embed credential env vars are no longer read unless `accept-env-vars` is enabled — this covers `query` and the whole `admin` command tree. BREAKING: the CLI-212 `NEO4J_DATABASE` override applied alongside `--credential` now also requires `accept-env-vars` (the explicit `--database` flag is unaffected). Stored credentials are never modified.
* `aura instance list` output now includes the instance `status`.
* Add `aura virtual-graph` commands for managing Aura Virtual Graphs in a project: `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `delete` and `allowed-configs`. `create` takes `--name`, `--data-source-id`, `--import-model-id`, `--cloud-provider` and `--region`, plus optional `--memory`, `--maximum-bytes-billed` and `--wait`, and prints the initial password once as `plain_password`. `list` returns every virtual graph in the project, following the API's pagination on your behalf; `--limit` caps how many are returned and notes on stderr when more exist

releases.name: v1.10.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **`aura graphql` commands are out of beta** — manage GraphQL Data APIs without flipping a hidden flag, with the full lifecycle plus auth providers and CORS allowed origins. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura graphql create --instance-id 00000000 --name my-api --memory 256MB --type-definitions-file ./typeDefs.graphql --rw
  ```

- **`--debug` everywhere it was missing** — route the underlying API/CLI activity to stderr (stdout stays clean) with secrets redacted, also togglable via `NEO4J_DEBUG=1`:
  - Aura commands echo HTTP request/response, token acquisition, and polling
  - `docker` commands echo the docker invocations they shell out to
  - `desktop` commands echo discovery probes and relate API traffic

- **`query --database` plays nicely with `--credential`** — point a saved or desktop credential at a specific database instead of whatever it shipped with. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli query "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n)" --credential desktop --database movies --format json
  ```

### Other changes

- `query`: `--database` now defaults to the connecting user's home database when unset rather than the literal "neo4j", fixing DatabaseNotFound errors on instances like AuraDB Free where home isn't named "neo4j".


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.10.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* Introduced `aura graphql` commands for managing GraphQL Data APIs: create, get, list, update, delete, pause, resume, auth-provider, and cors-policy allowed-origin.
* Aura commands now accept a --debug flag (also via NEO4J_DEBUG=1) that routes Aura API request/response activity to stderr with secrets redacted.
* Add --debug to docker commands to echo underlying docker invocations (secrets redacted) to stderr
* Add --debug to desktop commands (also via NEO4J_DEBUG=1) that routes Neo4j Desktop discovery and relate API request/response activity to stderr with secrets redacted
* query: --database flag and NEO4J_DATABASE env var can now be combined with --credential to target a specific database
### Patch
* query: --database now defaults to the connecting user's home database when unset instead of the literal "neo4j", fixing DatabaseNotFound errors against instances whose home database is not named "neo4j" (e.g. AuraDB Free, where it is the instance DBID).

releases.name: v1.9.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **`aura instance deploy` clones a local database into a fresh Aura instance** — dump an enterprise Neo4j database from a local Docker container or Neo4j Desktop 2 DBMS and push it straight into a brand-new instance, no manual export dance:
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura instance deploy --rw --from-docker my-local-neo4j --type free-db \
    --organization-id 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 \
    --project-id 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
  ```

- **Example datasets, loadable into any target** — `dataset list` surfaces curated suggestions (any GitHub repo with a manifest works), and per-target `load` commands drop a dataset into a Docker container, a Desktop DBMS, or a new Aura instance:
  ```
  neo4j-cli docker load neo4j-graph-examples/movies --name movies --wait --rw
  ```

- **Rendered output, tidied** — a consistency pass and a format fix for anyone parsing CLI output:
  - Rendered field names are now `snake_case` across docker, credential, workspace, and desktop commands (e.g. `bolt_port`, `database_name`, `organization_id`, `connection_uri`). **BREAKING**: scripts reading JSON/TOON keys or table headers must update. Flags, config keys, and Docker labels are unchanged.
  - Interactive terminals no longer revert to JSON — they default to table again, while AI agents default to TOON.

### Other changes

- Failing commands now tee their full redacted output to a file under the config dir (`neo4j/cli/tee`) and report its `tee_path` in the JSON/TOON error envelope; governed by the new `tee-enabled` and `tee-limit` config keys.
- `skill check` and `skill list` now report each catalog skill's version from that skill's own remote `SKILL.md`, not a single shared `plugin.json` version.
- `history list` and telemetry now report invoker `script` for non-TTY, non-agent runs (piped, CI, cron) — previously misreported as `agent`.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.9.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* Add `neo4j-cli aura instance deploy` to clone a local Neo4j database (from a managed Docker container or a Neo4j Desktop DBMS) into a new Aura instance.
* Failing commands now save their full redacted output to a tee file under the config directory (neo4j/cli/tee) and expose its path as tee_path in the JSON/toon error envelope; controlled by the new tee-enabled and tee-limit config keys.
* Rendered output field names are now snake_case across docker (bolt_port, http_port), credential (database_name, embed_credential, base_url, vertex_project, vertex_location), workspace (organization_id, project_id, project_name), and desktop (connection_uri, pending_restart, file_path) commands. BREAKING: scripts parsing JSON/TOON keys or table headers must update to the snake_case names. CLI flags, config keys, and Docker label identifiers are unchanged.
* Add `dataset list` and per-target `load` commands (`docker load`, `desktop dbms load`, `aura instance load`) to load example datasets from neo4j-graph-examples repos.
* Fix default output reverting to JSON instead of table in interactive terminals; default to TOON when run by an AI agent
### Patch
* `skill check` and `skill list` now report each catalog skill's available version from that skill's own remote SKILL.md `version:` instead of a single shared plugin.json version.
* neo4j-cli history list and telemetry now report invoker "script" for non-TTY, non-agent invocations (piped, CI, cron); these were previously reported as "agent".

releases.name: v1.8.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **`neo4j-cli query` runs multiple statements** — split a Cypher string on a line-ending `;` and run the lot in order; `--atomic` wraps them in one transaction that rolls back on failure, and `--continue-on-error` ploughs past failing statements in non-atomic mode. Write statements now report summary stats. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli query 'CREATE (:Person {name:"Alice"});
  CREATE (:Person {name:"Bob"})' --rw --atomic
  ```

- **`neo4j-cli history`** — a local log of recently run commands, so you can see what you (or an agent) actually ran. Secret flags are redacted; query Cypher is stored verbatim, so mind what you put in it. Toggle with `config set history-enabled`, cap with `history-limit`. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli history list --format json
  ```

- **`neo4j-cli desktop dbms upgrade`** — upgrade a Desktop-managed DBMS to a newer Neo4j version, picking the latest stable enterprise build when `--version` is omitted, with knobs for plugin migration, backups, and stopping a running DBMS first. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli desktop dbms upgrade my-dbms-id --version 5.26.1 --force --rw
  ```

### Other changes

- Desktop discovery now finds the Desktop 2 API via mDNS/DNS-SD even on non-standard or ephemeral ports, with the 44222..44232 port scan as fallback (`--port` if it still hides).
- Clearer signposting: the installer prints the GitHub issues URL, the bug-report link in error messages is fixed, and Bolt auth/connection plus embedding API-key errors now suggest a next step.
- `aura agent invoke` prints the agent invocation id on success and failure, for support and tracing.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.8.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* query: accept multiple statements separated by ; at line end; --atomic runs them in a single transaction; --continue-on-error keeps going past failing statements (non-atomic only); write statements now report summary stats (nodes/relationships/properties created, etc.); comment-only statements are skipped instead of erroring
* Clearer feedback signposting: the installer now prints the GitHub issues URL, the bug-report link in error messages is corrected, and Bolt auth/connection and embedding API-key errors now include actionable next-step suggestions.
* Add `neo4j-cli history` command (list, clear) that records a local log of recently run commands; secret flag values are redacted but query Cypher is stored verbatim. Toggle with `config set history-enabled` and cap with `history-limit`.
* desktop: discover the local Neo4j Desktop 2 API via mDNS/DNS-SD (_neo4j-desktop-2._tcp.local), so it's found even on non-standard or ephemeral ports; the 44222..44232 port scan remains a fallback. On macOS a dns-sd tier covers Local Network restrictions — if discovery still fails, pass --port.
* desktop: add `neo4j-cli desktop dbms upgrade <id>` to upgrade a Desktop-managed DBMS to a newer Neo4j version, with --plugin-upgrade-mode (all|none|upgradable, default upgradable), --version (auto-picks the latest stable enterprise version when omitted), --no-migrate, --backup, and --force.
* aura agent invoke now prints the agent invocation id on success and failure for support/tracing

releases.name: v1.7.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **Credentials move into the OS keyring** — new installs store secrets in the macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Store, or Linux Secret Service, with an opt-in switch for existing setups. Flipping the switch quietly migrates any plaintext credentials that are still hanging around in `credentials.json`, so partial state doesn't turn into a hard error. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli config set credential-storage keyring --rw
  ```

- **`skill install` now speaks to the curated skill catalog** — install any skill from the [neo4j-contrib/neo4j-skills](https://github.com/neo4j-contrib/neo4j-skills) catalog into the AI agents on your machine, with `--all`, `--refresh`, and a dedicated `skill refresh` leaf. Heads up: the positional argument is now the skill name (the previous agent-name positional is a hard error — use `--agent <name>`). Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli skill install neo4j-cypher-skill --rw
  ```

- **`aura tenant` and `--tenant-id` are gone** — deprecated since v1.4.0, finally removed. Use `aura project list` / `aura project get` for configuration details, `aura organization get` for org metadata, and `--project-id` everywhere you used to pass `--tenant-id`. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura project list --format json
  ```

### Other changes

- Added Gemini and Vertex AI embedding providers to `credential embed add` (`--provider gemini` and `--provider vertex`, the latter with `--vertex-project` / `--vertex-location`).
- Removed the deprecated `--await` alias; `--wait` is now the only spelling (CLI-111).
- The query skill's Virtual Graph forbidden-construct list now also covers `OPTIONAL MATCH`, vector search, and full-text search.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.7.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* Credentials are now stored securely in the OS keyring by default (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Store, Linux Secret Service). Existing credentials remain in plaintext until you run `neo4j-cli config set credential-storage keyring`. To keep plaintext storage, no action is required.
* 'neo4j-cli skill install <agent>' no longer accepts a positional agent name — use --agent <name> instead. New: install any skill from the curated neo4j-contrib/neo4j-skills catalog, plus --all, --refresh, and a new 'skill refresh' leaf.
* Removed deprecated --await alias; --wait is now the only spelling (CLI-111).
* Remove deprecated 'aura tenant list/get' commands and '--tenant-id' flag (deprecated in v1.4.0). Use 'aura project list', 'aura project get' (configuration details) or 'aura organization get' (org metadata), and '--project-id' instead.
* Added Gemini and Vertex AI embedding providers.
### Patch
* Credentials stored in plaintext JSON are silently used and automatically migrated to the OS keyring when credential-storage is set to keyring, preventing hard errors from out-of-sync state.
* Add OPTIONAL MATCH, vector and full-text search to the query skill's Virtual Graph forbidden-construct list

releases.name: v1.6.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **`desktop` subtree manages local Neo4j Desktop 2** — lifecycle local DBMSes, plugins, and saved remote connections without leaving the CLI, and let `query` borrow Desktop's credentials on demand. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli desktop list --format json
  ```

- **`--yes --force` gates every destructive leaf** — `*/delete` and `*/remove` commands (Aura instance/deployment/agent/CMK/data-api/graphanalytics/auth-provider/cors-policy allowed-origin, docker, desktop dbms/connection, credential aura-client/dbms/embed) now prompt y/N on a TTY and require both flags in non-TTY contexts. Back-compat break: `docker delete --force` (without `--yes`) and `desktop {dbms,connection} delete --yes` (without `--force`) now exit 2 in non-TTY shells. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura instance delete <id> --yes --force --rw
  ```

- **Query output polish** — two small but visible fixes for anyone parsing query results:
  - `:schema` now reports the active graph engine and supported Cypher versions via `dbms.components()`, and the query skill teaches agents which Cypher constructs to avoid on Virtual Graphs.
  - Temporal column values (Date, DateTime, Duration, …) render as ISO-8601 strings in JSON and table output instead of empty `{}`.

### Other changes

- Curl installer prompts to install the agent-skill bundle in a TTY; set `NEO4J_CLI_AUTO_INSTALL_SKILL=1` or `=0` for unattended installs.
- `skill install` now supports Antigravity CLI.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.6.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* Add 'neo4j-cli desktop' subtree for local Neo4j Desktop 2: 'desktop install' installs the app; 'desktop dbms' lifecycles local DBMSes (--wait on async leaves); 'desktop dbms plugin' manages plugins; 'desktop connection' manages saved remote connections; 'desktop list' shows both; 'desktop doctor' runs a structured health check. 'query --credential desktop' or 'desktop-connection:<uuid>' reads Desktop credentials on demand without writing them to the local store.
* Curl installer now prompts to install the agent-skill bundle when run in an interactive terminal; set NEO4J_CLI_AUTO_INSTALL_SKILL=1 or =0 for unattended installs.
* Gate destructive operations on a new --yes --force confirmation: every `*/delete` and `*/remove` leaf (aura instance/deployment/agent/customer-managed-key/data-api/graphanalytics/auth-provider/cors-policy allowed-origin, docker, desktop dbms/connection, credential aura-client/dbms/embed) now requires both flags in non-TTY contexts or prompts y/N on a TTY. Back-compat break: `docker delete --force` (without --yes) and `desktop {dbms,connection} delete --yes` (without --force) now exit 2 in non-TTY contexts; pass both flags going forward.
### Patch
* Add skill install support for Antigravity CLI.
* :schema now detects and reports the active graph engine (e.g. Virtual Graph) and supported Cypher versions via dbms.components(), and the query skill teaches agents which Cypher constructs to avoid on Virtual Graphs (CLI-177).
* Render temporal column values (Date, DateTime, Duration, ...) as ISO-8601 strings in query JSON and table output instead of empty {}.

releases.name: v1.5.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **Aura Agent commands land** — manage Aura agents end-to-end from the CLI: `list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `replace`, `delete`, `invoke`. Useful if you'd rather not poke the API by hand.
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura agent list --format json
  ```

- **`query --debug` plus a sane retry budget** — route Neo4j driver diagnostics (connection, auth, routing, retries) to stderr without touching stdout, so `--format json` stays pipe-clean. Driver `ConnectionAcquisitionTimeout` and `MaxTransactionRetryTime` are now capped at 10s on query commands, so a wrong URI scheme or port fails in seconds instead of looking like a hang.
  ```
  neo4j-cli query "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS n" --debug --format json
  ```

- **Friendlier errors across the board** — fewer Go-stringified mysteries when something goes wrong:
  - Next-action suggestions populated on Aura 400/401/403/404/429 and workspace/ownership errors.
  - Aura instance-type quota exhaustion (e.g. a second free-db) now surfaces an actionable suggestion instead of a bare conflict.
  - Aura API error bodies render in the same multi-line bracket format as auth errors, not Go's default `[]string` dump.
  - Panic diagnostics now show up in the panic-recovery line, so unhandled API status codes are actually diagnosable.

### Other changes

- `docker create --no-print-password` suppresses the generated password from stdout; retrieve it later via `credential dbms get`.
- `docker create` now validates `--version` against a charset allowlist before doing anything.
- `docker` redacts `NEO4J_AUTH` / `PASSWORD` values from docker stderr when surfacing errors.
- `update --force` prints a stderr warning and suggests switching to a self-managed install when it overrides package-manager detection.
- Added `SECURITY.md` documenting the update trust root.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.5.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* Populate next-action suggestions on Aura API errors (400/401/403/404/429) and workspace/ownership errors.
* Add Aura Agent: aura agent commands (list, get, create, update, replace, delete, invoke).
* Add --debug flag (and NEO4J_DEBUG=1 env var) on query commands to route Neo4j driver diagnostics to stderr, keeping --format json/toon stdout unaffected. Per-frame Bolt wire tracing (BoltLogger) is a deliberate follow-up pending credential redaction.
* Cap Neo4j driver ConnectionAcquisitionTimeout and MaxTransactionRetryTime at 10s on query commands so interactive failures (e.g. wrong URI scheme/port) surface within seconds instead of the driver's 1m / 30s defaults that read as a hang.
* docker create: --no-print-password suppresses generated password from stdout output (CLI-161)
### Patch
* Surface an actionable suggestion when an Aura instance-type quota is exceeded (e.g. attempting to create a free-db when one already exists), and surface any panic diagnostic in the CLI's panic-recovery line so unhandled API status codes are diagnosable.
* Aura API error messages now render in the same multi-line bracket format used for auth errors instead of Go's default []string stringification.
* docker create: validate --version against allowlist (CLI-160)
* docker: redact NEO4J_AUTH/PASSWORD values in error messages from docker stderr (CLI-162)
* docs: add SECURITY.md documenting update trust root (CLI-158)
* update: warn on stderr and suggest switching to a self-managed install when --force overrides package-manager detection (CLI-157)

releases.name: v1.4.0
releases.body:
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **A `docker` command tree for local Neo4j containers** — spin up, list, and tear down Neo4j containers without remembering the right `docker run` incantation. Containers are discovered via the `org.neo4j.cli.managed=true` label, so Docker itself is the source of truth — no parallel state file to drift. `create` does port-pair auto-increment when 7687/7474 are taken and matches stored dbms credentials so `neo4j-cli query` connects out of the box. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli docker create --name dev --rw
  ```

- **Aura is now organized by organization and project, not tenant** — `aura tenant list/get` are hidden and slated for removal; `aura organization`, `aura project`, and `aura workspace` are the replacement. Pick a default workspace once and every instance, customer-managed-key, and graph-analytics command picks the right project. `--organization-id` and `--project-id` flags resolve the target, and `--tenant-id` is deprecated in favour of `--project-id`. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura workspace use <org-id>/<project-id> --rw
  ```

- **Structured error envelopes when `--format=json` or `--format=toon`** — failed commands now emit a parseable error object on stdout instead of a free-form string, so scripts and agents can branch on the failure code without regex-scraping. The human one-liner still goes to stderr; exit codes are unchanged. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli aura instance get does-not-exist --format json
  ```

- **`upgrade` alias and universal "did you mean" suggestions** — `neo4j-cli upgrade` now works as a synonym for `update`, and a typo at any level of the command tree gets a suggestion list and an exit code 2 instead of a silent help dump. Example:
  ```
  neo4j-cli upgrade
  ```

### Other changes

- Feature-flag registry added; `aura.beta-enabled` renamed to `flag.aura-beta` (legacy key still read until CLI-134).
- `docker create` auto-increments both host ports by the same offset when the requested bolt/http pair is taken.
- Removed residual aura-cli source and build artifacts (standalone entrypoint, skill bundle subsystem, dead workflow gating, stale docs).
- Whitespace is now trimmed from positional ID args in the remaining aura subcommands.
- Unknown subcommands exit 2 (usage_error) at every nesting level instead of falling through to a help dump with the wrong exit code.


---

## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v1.4.0

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* Add 'docker' command tree for managing local Neo4j containers (CLI-123)
* Add organization list/get, project list/get, and workspace list/use commands; replace config project subsystem with aura.default-workspace key; deprecate aura tenant list/get (use project list and organization get instead — removal planned for a future release)
* docker create: auto-increment host ports when defaults are taken (CLI-131)
* Aura workspace is now applied to all instance, customer-managed-key, and graph-analytics session commands; --organization-id and --project-id flags resolve the target project and --tenant-id is deprecated in favour of --project-id
* Add feature-flag registry; rename aura.beta-enabled to flag.aura-beta (legacy key still read until CLI-134)
* Emit structured error envelope to stdout when --format=json or --format=toon and a command fails (CLI-140)
### Patch
* Add 'upgrade' alias for the update command and 'did you mean' suggestions for typo'd subcommands
* Remove residual aura-cli source/build artifacts (standalone entrypoint, skill bundle subsystem, dead workflow gating, stale docs).
* Trim whitespace from positional ID args in remaining aura subcommands (CLI-139)
* Unknown subcommands now exit 2 (usage_error) at every nesting level instead of falling through to a help dump with the wrong exit code.

releases.body:
## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v0.1.0-alpha.3
- aura-cli: v2.0.0-alpha.2

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* analytics: emit command-specific events for aura (AURA), query (QUERY), and skill (SKILL) commands; query events record only the command name to prevent capturing query content or credentials that may contain PII, and include an is_aura flag derived from the --uri value
* Add toon output format option (--format toon / -f toon)
### Patch
* analytics: simplify Service interface — removed EmitStartupEvent, EmitCommandEvent, EmitHelpEvent, Enable, and IsEnabled; EmitEvent now accepts an event suffix and always injects base properties at send time

### aura-cli

### Minor
* Add toon output format option (--format toon / -f toon)

releases.name: v0.1.0-alpha.2
releases.body:
## Versions

- neo4j-cli: v0.1.0-alpha.2
- aura-cli: v2.0.0-alpha.1

## Changes

### neo4j-cli

### Minor
* Add top-level `neo4j config` commands (`config get`, `config set`, `config list`) supporting dot-notation keys (e.g. `neo4j config get aura.base-url`, `neo4j config get output`)
* `--output` flag now applies uniformly to config and credential commands; `aura credential list` now renders as a table by default with `name`, `type`, and `identifier` columns (sensitive fields omitted)
* `neo4j aura config` has been removed; use `neo4j config aura` instead
* Add `skill` subcommand to install agent skills into supported AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.)
* `neo4j-cli` is now installable via `npm i -g @neo4j-labs/cli`
* Add 'query' command to run Cypher against a Neo4j database via the HTTP Query API
* query/:schema: auto-detect piped/redirected stdout and default --output to json
* query/:schema: send a User-Agent header (neo4j-cli/v<version>) so server logs identify the CLI
* Renamed `--output` to `--format` and added `-f` as a shorthand
* distribute via Homebrew: install with `brew install neo4j-labs/tap/neo4j-cli` (formula auto-generated by GoReleaser on stable releases)
### Patch
* Remove leftover debug log lines (help displayed, invalid command with args, command executed successfully) that were printed to stdout from the CLI entrypoint

### aura-cli

### Minor
* `--output` flag now applies uniformly to config and credential commands; `aura credential list` now renders as a table by default with `name`, `type`, and `identifier` columns (sensitive fields omitted)
* Add `skill` subcommand to install agent skills into supported AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.)
* Renamed `--output` to `--format` and added `-f` as a shorthand
### Patch
* Remove leftover debug log lines (help displayed, invalid command with args, command executed successfully) that were printed to stdout from the CLI entrypoint
